requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.authoring.usage_storage` has no implementation roots or implementation edges, and I found no structural obligation that needs one. It names no library, algorithm, function signature, type, field-ownership rule or delegation interface. Each clause describes observable behavior, and a different build would still satisfy it:

- "separate JSON usage record under `<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`": this sets the file location and format. A hand-built `serde_json::json!` map, or a differently named struct, writes the same file. The state root comes from `requirements.configuration.state_location`, which this text only cites. The path rules live in that requirement's own text.
- "MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome, accepted determination kind … and whether evidence was written": this lists what the JSON contains. It names no Rust type. Any serializer that emits those keys meets it.
- "`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`", "a successful write to either destination MUST set `evidence_written` to true", "Usage recording MUST remain outside the project in stdout mode", "FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored", "Failed, cancelled, or unfinished runs MUST remain distinguishable" and "without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale": these are conditions on the written output and on where it is written. A test can observe each one, and none says how the code must be organized.

The requirement has test edges, which supply evidence for these behavioral obligations. A structural obligation would be a mandated type, library or delegation, and I found none. I searched for `evidence_output` only to see how it appears. I did not rely on any of the hits.

behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap. I did not read the implementation source. Each obligation maps to a marked test, as follows.

- **Separate record per assessment at `<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`, using the state-location rules.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported]` checks that the file lives under `<state>/habeas/authoring/usage`, is named `<run_id>.json`, and is left byte-identical by a second run, which creates a second file. It also checks that an undeterminable or uncreatable state location fails the run, reports an error and writes no evidence.
  - `fn[confirm_runs_a_second_assessment_with_its_own_usage_record]`, `fn[adaptive_routes_fresh_assessments_and_records_each_model]` and `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citation_reviews_are_confirmed_with_fresh_targeted_conversations]` check that separate assessments get separate records with distinct `run_id` values.
  - The batch tests in `tests/authoring_batch.rs` check that each assessment has one record: 6 records for 6 subjects, 8 after the reauthoring runs.
- **Required fields.**
  - `fn[usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported]` asserts `version`, `run_id`, the canonical `project_root`, `subject`, `subject_kind`, `backend`, `model`, `evidence_output` and the start and end times.
  - `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[usage_subject_kind_is_known_before_sources_are_prepared]` covers the requirement, example, citation review and site review kinds.
  - `fn[usage_record_of_an_early_failure_identifies_its_subject_kind]` checks the subject kind on an early failure.
  - `src/authoring/usage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unfinished_runs_are_visible_before_the_backend_is_selected]` checks that backend, model and end time are null when not yet known.
- **Determination kinds.** `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` asserts `determination` is `true`, `false` and `FIXME` for each case. `fn[false_is_a_completed_assessment]` and `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` assert `false` and `FIXME`. The failure tests assert a null `determination` when none was accepted.
- **`evidence_output` and `evidence_written`.** File mode is asserted as `file` with `evidence_written` true in the ollama CLI test. Stdout mode is asserted as `stdout` with `evidence_written` true in the stdout test and the live Bedrock test. Failed submissions assert the correct `evidence_output` and `evidence_written` false in both modes, in `fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]`. `fn[failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage]` covers a failed write that keeps the accepted determination and sets `evidence_written` false.
- **Usage stays outside the project in stdout mode.** `fn[usage_state_inside_the_project_is_refused_before_creating_it]` runs with and without `--stdout`. It checks that the run is refused with a specific error and that the directory inside the project is never created. The stdout test checks that project files are unchanged.
- **No FIXME entry text.** The ollama CLI test uses the entry `example/app#125` and asserts that `#125` is absent from the serialized usage record.
- **Failed, cancelled and unfinished runs are distinguishable.**
  - Unfinished is asserted in `fn[unfinished_runs_are_visible_before_the_backend_is_selected]`.
  - Failed is asserted in many tests, including the failed-assessment batch test, the denied-mandatory-input test and the invalid-submission tests.
  - Failed versus cancelled is asserted in `fn[failed_persistence_records_failure_or_cancellation_and_retains_the_cause]`, which also checks a null `determination`, `evidence_written` false and a non-null end time.
  - Completed is asserted in the success tests.
- **No stored source text, prompts, responses or rationale, and persistence for later review.** The ollama CLI test plants `SECRET_*` markers in the requirement, definition, source payload and rationale. It asserts none appears in the usage JSON, and it also checks that the credential is absent. The usage records are re-read from disk in later steps and compared byte for byte.

Citation review and site review subject kinds are asserted at the unit level by `kind_noun`, which is cross-checked against the kind the prepared sources record. The requirement text does not require more per-kind assertions.

text: :::{req} usage_storage
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
:::{req} state_location
Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
